claims.statement: The repository-root Claude marketplace lists exactly one plugin, named powercontext, sourced from integrations/claude-code/plugins/powercontext at version 0.1.3, and the plugin manifest declares user options server_url, capture_prompts, and allow_insecure_http without declaring hooks or mcpServers.

The plugin's hooks.json registers exactly two events, SessionStart (matcher startup|resume|clear|compact|fork) and UserPromptSubmit (no matcher), each running python3 in exec form against a script under ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks with a 10 second timeout; no Stop or PreToolUse hook is registered.

The MCP configuration is a top-level powercontext HTTP server at ${user_config.server_url}/mcp whose only header is Authorization set from ${POWERCONTEXT_CLAUDE_AUTHORIZATION:-}, so the Claude plugin uses environment expansion rather than a headers helper.

powercontext setup claude-code adds or updates the powercontext marketplace and installs or updates powercontext@powercontext at user scope through the claude CLI, refusing to reuse a marketplace whose source differs from the requested one.

Setup merges server_url and allow_insecure_http (and capture_prompts when supplied) into the plugin's pluginConfigs options in Claude Code settings.json, leaving unrelated settings intact, and installs a python3 status line command only when no status line exists or the existing one is a PowerContext statusline.py.

Scope resolution always goes through the Server: the plugin sends POST /v1/scope-bindings/resolve with explicit_scope_id set from POWERCONTEXT_CLAUDE_SCOPE_ID (or null) and an ordered binding_keys list holding a session key when a session_id exists followed by a workspace key; the plugin never generates a Scope ID locally.
The Server resolves a Scope in this order: an explicit Scope ID, which must exist; then the first binding key with a stored binding; then the Server's default Scope.

When POWERCONTEXT_CLAUDE_SCOPE_ID is unset, Scope resolution falls back to a stored session binding, then a stored workspace binding, then the Server default Scope; if no default Scope exists the Server returns 404 scope_not_found, and because the UserPromptSubmit scope resolution is outside recall's suppression the hook exits silently with neither recall nor capture.

The workspace binding key is the SHA-256 of the Git top-level path (or the working directory when Git is unavailable or fails), and it is never derived from a Git remote or directory name; the session key uses the trimmed session_id limited to 256 characters.

Workspace bindings are managed explicitly: --bind-scope issues PUT /v1/scope-bindings and requires the Server to echo the same Scope ID, --clear-scope posts to /v1/scope-bindings/clear, and the Server's bind operation rejects a Scope that does not exist before writing the binding.

Each UserPromptSubmit invocation resolves the Scope, loads and then clears the session's bootstrap receipt, scrubs secrets and bounds the recall query, sends at most one POST /v1/context/prepare, injects returned content as additionalContext, and captures the prompt independently as a Content Source.

Prompt capture posts the unmodified prompt to /v1/sources/content only when capture is enabled and the prompt is at most 200,000 characters; capture is skipped with reason sensitive_content when the secret scrubber alters the prompt, and the capture request is never rewritten.

The captured Source has a deterministic ID derived from the SHA-256 of scope, session, prompt ID, and prompt text, so repeated identical captures in the same session and Scope are idempotent, and prompt capture never writes Memory or labels the prompt as a task outcome.

Flush-on-capture is opt-in: when enabled, the hook calls POST /v1/memory/flush up to flush_max_calls times until the reported current_cursor reaches the captured Source position, and failure to reach it is reported as a flush failure.

A recall query is the trimmed prompt when it fits 8,192 characters and 8,192 UTF-8 bytes; a longer prompt keeps its most recent text, cut to the last 8,192 characters and then 8,192 bytes without splitting a character.

The Hook accepts a Prepared Context only when the response has exactly schema, status, content, and content_bytes, the schema is powercontext.prepared-context.v1, empty responses carry no content, and ready responses carry non-blank content whose byte length matches content_bytes and does not exceed 8,000 bytes; any other shape is rejected.

Secret scrubbing for the recall query removes PEM private-key blocks, common credential assignments and bearer or provider tokens, and the active Authorization credential, and it is best-effort recognition rather than a guarantee.

Failure classification for recall maps HTTP 401 to authentication_failed, a 404 without an error code on the prepare path to version_mismatch, HTTP 503 or unreachable or timed-out Servers to server_unavailable, and other statuses or invalid payloads to invalid_response, and the hook injects nothing in these cases.

Diagnostics are content-free and throttled: they never contain the prompt, Scope ID, prepared content, Authorization value, or response body; each failure outcome is emitted at most once per process and is cooled down for 60 seconds across hook processes.

HTTP requests from the plugin refuse redirects, cap response bodies at 1 MiB, and clamp every socket read to one absolute deadline, with a shared six-second Hook budget and three-second per-request default timeout.

The effective Server URL resolves from POWERCONTEXT_CLAUDE_SERVER_URL, then the explicit entry-point URL, the plugin option, the saved client setting, and the default http://127.0.0.1:8000; plaintext HTTP is accepted only for loopback hosts unless allow_insecure_http is set, and URLs with credentials, queries, or fragments are rejected.

Authorization is environment-sourced: the Hook reads POWERCONTEXT_CLAUDE_AUTHORIZATION or a stored credential file matched to the same Server URL, while the MCP configuration reads only the environment variable; the value must be a single Bearer credential.

SessionStart bootstrap is opt-in and two-phase: it posts /v1/context/bootstrap with profile powercontext.scope-bootstrap.v1 for the five lifecycle sources, claims the returned receipt with an injected outcome, and only then saves a content-free local receipt and writes additionalContext; a failed claim posts a failed outcome and emits nothing.

The bootstrap receipt is stored under CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA in a file named by the SHA-256 of the session ID, holds only scope and receipt identifiers, is written with mode 0600 through an atomic replace, and is ignored when its permissions or shape are invalid.

The plugin does not register a Stop hook, does not read the transcript, and does not capture Claude's final response; durable Memory and Handoff writes happen only through explicit MCP operations, so automatic recall does not depend on MCP usage.

Compared with the Codex plugin, the Claude Code plugin registers fewer hook events (no PreToolUse tool binding and no Stop token-savings hook), runs python3 with the standard library instead of uv run, and does not use an http_headers_helper for MCP authorization.
